comment: Mutation testing for the SHIPPED RUNTIME assembly. A THIRD config because Stryker mutates one 'project' per run. Registry members, MapConfig, the IDwarfMapper facade and the exception types have no derivable case-space the way an attribute does — there is no AttributeUsage to decompose and no endpoint matrix to cross them against — so a surviving mutant is the only non-textual proof that a case is untested. This is what makes AmbiguousInterfaces and DestinationType (zero references in any test family, round 18) impossible rather than merely noticed. Run via scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation, and in CI via the 'runtime-mutation' job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (needs: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.16.0). MEASURED 2026-08-17 on Stryker 4.16.0: score 61.02 % (72 killed of 118 scoreable; 39 survived, 7 uncovered, 8 compile errors excluded), 2 min 50 s wall-clock on 12 cores. break is that score rounded DOWN to 61. WHY THE NUMBER WENT DOWN, AND WHY 66 MUST NOT BE 'RESTORED': the previous value (66, from a measured 66.95 % on 2026-08-16) was INFLATED, not regressed. That run took 44 minutes because every mutant re-ran essentially the whole 5,592-test suite serially, and 11 mutants were recorded as detected via TIMEOUT with an EMPTY killedBy — i.e. credited to the clock rather than to any assertion. Scoping the leg (below) made the run fast, and 7 of those 11 immediately showed their true status of Survived. They are not lost kills: FOUR of them delete 'ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull' calls (DwarfMapperRegistry lines 200-202) or turn 'Source.GetHashCode() * 397' into '/ 397' (line 301) — mutations with no loop, no recursion and no blocking call, which CANNOT hang, so a Timeout was never a genuine detection for them. ONE of them (DwarfRefContext line 77, 'maxDepth < 1' mutated to 'maxDepth <= 1') is a provably EQUIVALENT mutant: the two forms differ only at maxDepth == 1 and agree there anyway, since the original falls through 'maxDepth > AbsoluteMaxDepth' (1000) and also yields 1. No test can EVER detect it, yet 66.95 % counted it as detected. The bias has a mechanism: Stryker's bail is on by default, so a mutant WITH a killer aborts its session at the first failing test while a mutant nothing kills must run all 5,589 covering tests to completion — the slowest session, and therefore the one most likely to time out. The old Timeout bucket thus preferentially collected SURVIVORS and reported them as detected. Corroborated in reverse: four other baseline Timeouts (registry lines 68-70, DwarfRefContext line 78 equality) came back cleanly KILLED with named killers once the run was fast. 61.02 % is the honest score of the SAME 111 tested mutants and is the number a future regression must be measured against; treat 61 as the ratchet floor and raise it only by killing survivors. SCOPING MECHANISM — 'test-case-filter': of the 5,592 tests Stryker discovered, only 288 (5.2 %, in 23 classes) ever kill a mutant of this assembly; the rest 'cover' it only because DwarfMapperRegistry is a process-wide static populated by module initializers and DwarfRefContext is threaded through every reference-preserving map. coverage-analysis: perTest measures TOUCH, not INTENT, so it cannot narrow that. The filter names those 23 classes explicitly, derived from every killedBy in the 2026-08-16 report rather than guessed — an earlier hand-written list of 7 would have lost 18 kills. 'FullyQualifiedName~' is a contains-match, so the filter can only ever OVER-include, which is the score-safe direction. Note test-case-filter is absent from 'dotnet stryker --help' but is a real 4.16 key (it sits beside test-projects in Stryker.CLI.dll's key table and is consumed by Stryker.TestRunner.VsTest.dll). Full derivation and per-class kill counts: Issues/ledgers/E3-E1-report.md. NOTE 1: 'comment' lives OUTSIDE the 'stryker-config' object because Stryker 4.16 REJECTS unknown keys inside it — the two sibling configs kept theirs inside and could not run at all until this was found. NOTE 2: the 'mutate' globs must NOT be repo-root-relative. Stryker resolves them against the PROJECT directory (src/DwarfMapper), so 'src/DwarfMapper/Foo.cs' matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0 — a vacuous run that housekeeping's $LASTEXITCODE check cannot detect. That is exactly what the first measured run of this file did, and it is why Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1, mirrored in the CI job) counts scoreable statuses in the JSON report instead of trusting the exit code. NOTE 3: 'test-projects' is INERT here — do not add entries expecting an effect. Stryker discovers the solution (DwarfMapper.NET.sln) and enumerates EVERY test project in it, so this list does not select the test set; test-case-filter is what does. Proof: the 2026-08-16 run executed all 5,592 tests across seven test projects even though this list named two, and DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests classes appear in killedBy — a test that never ran cannot kill. The list is kept only as documentation of which projects contain killers. NOTE 4: an earlier version of this comment claimed excluding DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests cost ZERO killed mutants, on the grounds that DwarfMapValidationException's constructors are bare ': base(...)' forwarders producing no mutants. That claim is FALSE and was measured on a run in which the exclusion never took effect (see NOTE 3), so it measured nothing. Generator.Tests holds three killer classes — TopologyOracleFuzzTests, CrossConfigFuzzTests and AutoValidateRuntimeTests — accounting for 37 kill events, of which 8 are EXCLUSIVE: registry line 87, and DwarfRefContext lines 77 (x2), 83, 88, 114 and 130 (x2). Genuinely excluding that project would drop the score to 60.17 %. It is therefore listed in test-projects and its three classes are in the filter. Its non-exclusion is also part of why the unscoped run took 44 minutes: 4,601 of the 5,592 tests are Generator.Tests', and they were all running.
